page_title: Sleepless: keep your Mac awake with the lid closed

summary.name: Sleepless
summary.one_liner: Sleepless is an open-source (MIT) native macOS menu-bar app that keeps a MacBook awake with the lid closed, on battery, without an external display, by toggling pmset disablesleep.
use_cases: Keep a MacBook awake with the lid closed for downloads or syncs
Run an unattended build, render, or training job with the lid shut
Share a hotspot from a closed MacBook on battery
Stop a keep-awake session automatically before battery runs flat
Replace caffeinate-based keep-awake apps for lid-closed use
summary.what_it_does: Sleepless adds a menu-bar switch that toggles pmset disablesleep, which overrides lid-close sleep, and reads the flag back so the icon reflects the real state. It offers a 1 or 2 hour auto-off timer with a live countdown, and a battery floor from 5 to 50% (default 15%) that turns it off before the battery runs flat. If Low Power Mode is on while on battery, it releases the setting and lets the Mac sleep. The installer adds a sudoers rule permitting exactly two pmset commands so no password prompt is needed. Releases include SHA-256 sums and a Sigstore build-provenance attestation.
notable: Uses pmset disablesleep, the lower-level setting that can override lid-close sleep, unlike power-assertion tools
Single AppKit file with no daemon, kernel extension, or dependencies; no telemetry or network calls
Releases signed with Sigstore build provenance and SHA-256 checksums; scoped sudoers grant limited to two exact commands
Battery floor cutoff and Low Power Mode awareness
caveats: Apple does not officially document pmset disablesleep, and behavior depends on hardware and macOS version
Heavy sustained load with the lid closed reduces airflow; the page advises judgement
Requires a one-time sudo grant via the installer
